questions.exp: Discharge: Adequate pain control with a supply of oral analgesia. (Book p27)

questions.q: ERAS protocol stands for:
questions.exp: ERAS protocol (Enhanced recovery after Sx). (Book p27)

questions.exp: ERAS Preoperative: Patient counselling & expectations; Avoid mechanical bowel preparation. (Book p27)

questions.q: Preoperative ERAS advises to:
questions.exp: ERAS Preoperative: Avoid mechanical bowel preparation. (Book p27)

questions.q: As per ERAS, solids are allowed up to:
questions.exp: ERAS: Solids up to 6 hours prior to Sx. (Book p27)

questions.q: As per ERAS, carbohydrate loading is done:
questions.exp: ERAS: Carbohydrate loading: 2 to 3 hours before Sx. (Book p27)

questions.q: As per ERAS, clear liquids are allowed up to:
questions.exp: ERAS: Clear liquids up to 2 hours prior to Sx. (Book p27)

questions.q: Preoperative ERAS considers all of the following EXCEPT:

questions.q: Intraoperative ERAS prefers a:

questions.q: Intraoperative ERAS uses local anesthetic or long acting local like:
questions.exp: ERAS: Local anesthetic or long acting local (liposomal bupivacaine). (Book p27)

questions.q: Intraoperative ERAS advises to:

questions.q: ERAS prophylaxis for nausea & vomiting must cover at least:
questions.exp: ERAS: Prophylaxis for nausea & vomiting (At least 2 classes of medications). (Book p27)

questions.q: Which drug is listed 'if appropriate' intraoperatively in ERAS?

questions.q: Postoperative ERAS analgesia uses:

questions.q: As per ERAS, IV fluids are discontinued:

units.title: Definition & Day-Care Examples
units.guide: Day care means in and out within 12 hours - from haemorrhoids, hernias and lap cholecystectomy to breast biopsy, TURP, carpal tunnel release and varicose vein procedures.

units.title: Selection: Medical Criteria
units.guide: Physiological age trumps chronological age: ASA I-II patients suit stand-alone centres while ASA III needs a hospital unit, with BMI capped at 38 for laparoscopic and 40 for surface procedures.

units.title: Selection: Diabetes, Social & Surgical
units.guide: Diabetics under HbA1C 8.5 skip the morning OHA, blood pressure stays below 180/100, and epilepsy must be well controlled. Behind every day-care patient stands a responsible adult for 24 hours, a suitable home, operations under 2 hours, and a quick return to eating and drinking.

units.title: Scheduling & Anaesthesia
units.guide: Comorbid patients get priority in stand-alone units, and day cases lead mixed lists. Propofol TIVA keeps nausea away while bupivacaine infiltration handles the pain.

units.title: Post-op Complications
units.guide: Haemorrhage - primary during surgery, reactionary within 4-24 hours, secondary days later from infection - is the commonest cause of re-admission. PONV, predicted by the Apfel score, is the commonest complication overall, followed by pain.

units.title: Discharge Criteria
units.guide: Discharge demands an hour of stable vitals, full orientation, controlled pain with oral analgesia in hand, the ability to dress and walk, minimal nausea or bleeding, sips of fluid, passed urine, a responsible escort, clear written and verbal instructions, a follow-up plan and an emergency number.

units.title: ERAS Protocol
units.guide: ERAS fast-tracks recovery: counselled patients skip bowel prep, take solids till 6 hours and carb drinks till 2-3 hours, glide through minimally invasive surgery kept warm with multimodal antiemetics, then eat, walk and leave IV fluids behind - all within 24 hours on non-opioid analgesia.
